plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, the 4-date timeline completes: Dec 1987 (Yoshizumi Ishino discovers 29-bp palindromic repeats and 32-bp spacers in E. coli) · Feb 2005 (Francisco Mojica proves CRISPR spacers match bacteriophage viruses) · 23 Mar 2007 (Rodolphe Barrangou & Philippe Horvath prove yogurt bacteria use CRISPR-Cas9 as an adaptive immune system) · 28 Jun 2012 (Emmanuelle Charpentier & Jennifer Doudna engineer programmable single-guide RNA CRISPR-Cas9 scissors; first human CRISPR cure approved Nov 2023).

teach_overlay.detail: Animated 4-date timeline (Dec 1987 → 28 Jun 2012 / Nov 2023) alongside the ex-vivo adult hematopoietic stem-cell editing cure for sickle-cell disease
teach_overlay.scale: just twenty-five years separated Yoshizumi Ishino's puzzling bacterial repeats in nineteen eighty-seven from programmable DNA scissors in twenty twelve — and eleven years after that, the first human patients were cured of sickle-cell disease
